text:
A: Hiya. So I told the last one it was my last one. Turns out I can't count.
B: Oh, hello. Sorry, I'm Joanne. I think this is the last one, isn't it? I'm not sure.
A: It's definitely the last one. Probably. Leanne. Stockport.
B: Basingstoke. I clean on the wards, at the hospital.
A: Right. Early starts?
B: Half five. I'm a bit shattered, sorry, if I'm quiet.
A: You're fine. I'm loud enough for both of us, apparently. I'm a graphic designer. Menus, shop signs, that kind of thing. And my own prints.
B: Oh, I saw them on your wall. I wouldn't know what to say about them, sorry. I'm not very arty.
A: You don't have to say anything about them. Most people who do say the wrong thing anyway. Do you like them or not?
B: Erm, I liked the blue one. With the bird.
A: That's a heron. That's the one that sold out. So you've got taste, actually.
B: Oh. Well. I don't know about that.
A: Take it, I don't say it much. Do you get much hydro at your hospital? I do hydrotherapy, I've got rheumatoid arthritis.
B: We've got a hydro pool, yes. I don't do that bit, but I clean near it sometimes. The physios are lovely. Sorry, that must be hard, the arthritis.
A: Some days. I used to skate roller derby. Now I do slow lengths with pensioners. Who are faster than me, which is humbling.
B: My mum's seventy-eight. She had a fall last winter. I worry about her all the time, if I'm honest.
A: Does she live on her own?
B: Yes. She won't move. She says she's fine. I ring her every night and she says I'm fussing.
A: Mine rings me every Sunday at tea time. Without fail. Middle of eating, every time.
B: That's nice, though. That she rings.
A: Yeah. It is, I suppose. Don't tell her I said that.
B: I won't. Sorry, is that a crayon drawing behind you? No, sorry, that's mine. On my fridge. I thought it was your screen for a second.
A: Ha. Who did it?
B: My grandson. He's two. It's meant to be Biscuit, the cat. It looks like a potato.
A: Honestly, that's better than half the logos I get sent. Clients would pay for that.
B: Oh, stop it. He'd be chuffed, though.
A: I'm serious. Bold line, no faff. He's got more confidence than most designers.
B: I'll tell Kirsty. She'll laugh.
A: You're not what I expected, you know. I thought you'd be —
